content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near-zero — model ignores downside risk, leading to persistent underprediction.
- Lag in correction: model often fails to adjust forecast downward after a sharp price spike, especially if sentiment was positive in prior days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, failing to revert to historical mean in medium-term horizon (30d) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Overshoot after sentiment reversal: if sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model continues upward trend, leading to overprediction in later days.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early days of forecast window — model often peaks too early and then drops, especially when sentiment is volatile.
